pure-announcement.rationale: It is a research note analyzing an attack class, with no product launch or release content anywhere in it.

duplicate.rationale: remote-first-mcp-governance names tool-poisoning risk only as a one-line motivator; no existing concept covers the attack mechanism, its rug-pull and shadowing variants, or the pin-and-verify defenses detailed here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Central claims are anchored to checkable artifacts — CVE-2025-54136 and CVE-2025-6514 in NVD, Invariant Labs' reproducible PoC repo, and the MCPTox arXiv benchmark.

durability.rationale: The core finding is structural — server-supplied tool metadata enters the agent's context with instruction-level authority and no integrity verification — and the note itself argues this survives individual CVE patches, so the mechanism and its defenses will hold in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes specific controls a deploying team can implement now: SHA-256 pinning of tool manifests with re-verification at session init, server allowlists, treating tool-returned content as untrusted, gateway-level manifest inspection, and behavioral baselining.

atomicity.rationale: The variants (description poisoning, rug pull, shadowing, supply chain) are explicitly framed as one attack class with a single structural cause, statable in one paragraph, with the framework-alignment section as supporting apparatus rather than separate ideas.
